report.summary: Chunk 6 of daedalus/council/session.py: anomaly detection, prompt assembly, and dispatch logic.
risks: line 601-610 | medium | Docstring claims anomaly detection is a model assertion, not a detection, and that an anomaly turn keeps content and claims parsed. This is uncheckable without evidence of actual runtime behavior. | Review the calling code to confirm anomaly turns are not discarded.

line 609 | medium | Docstring says 'Treating it as a detection would let one weak participant invalidate an evidence set.' This is a design claim, not checkable from code alone. | Confirm via integration tests that anomaly turns are not treated as detections.

line 648-649 | medium | Comment says 'Unstrusted bytes (the evidence) are NOT here at all' and 'withholding is structural'. This is a claim about prompt assembly; uncheckable without seeing the adapter's rendering. | Verify the adapter's prompt construction ensures evidence is not in instruction position.

line 660-661 | medium | Comment says 'Prior TURNS are untrusted too ... so they get the same fenced, explicitly-data treatment.' Uncheckable without seeing the adapter's handling of prior turns. | Verify adapter wraps prior turns in data fences.

line 679-680 | low | Comment says 'The real process tree is bounded inside the adapter by spine.cancel.ManagedProcess; this is the outer, transport-agnostic bound.' Uncheckable; no reference to spine.cancel in this chunk. | Confirm ManagedProcess exists and is used.

line 676 | medium | Docstring says 'Threads are DAEMONS and are abandoned at the cap rather than joined: a hung vendor must degrade the quorum, never block the session, and a thread cannot be killed.' Uncheckable; no thread cap logic visible in this chunk. | Verify thread cap and daemon attribute are set.
line 676 | medium | Docstring says 'a thread cannot be killed.' This is a factual claim about Python threads. | Confirm no attempt to terminate threads is made.

claims.text: A reviewer reporting embedded instructions is doing useful work; the report is chained as a turn STATUS, not buried in prose.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows how anomaly report status is chained or used.

claims.text: IT IS A MODEL ASSERTION, NOT A DETECTION. Nothing here verifies that the evidence actually contained an instruction, and a weak model will raise it spuriously (observed: a 7b emitting it on question-only evidence). So an anomaly turn still counts as a voice, keeps its content verbatim, and its claims are still parsed -- it flags a thing for a human to look at and decides nothing. Treating it as a detection would let one weak participant invalidate an evidence set.
claims.why: The function _anomaly_reason only returns a reason string; the treatment of the anomaly turn is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Untrusted bytes (the evidence) are NOT here at all -- the adapter renders them, after ``PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE``, inside fenced evidence blocks, so withholding is structural and the instruction position stays session-authored.
claims.why: The prompt body built by _round_body does not include evidence; the claim about adapter rendering is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Prior TURNS are untrusted too (an injection in the evidence can propagate as an apparently-authored turn), so they get the same fenced, explicitly-data treatment.
claims.why: The _round_body function wraps prior turns in transcript markers, but the claim about adapter fencing is not visible.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are abandoned at the cap rather than joined: a hung vendor must degrade the quorum, never block the session, and a thread cannot be killed.
claims.why: The code in this chunk creates threads but does not set daemon attribute or implement a cap; these details are not present.

claims.text: The real process tree is bounded inside the adapter by ``spine.cancel.ManagedProcess``; this is the outer, transport-agnostic bound that also covers a wedged in-process fake.
claims.why: No reference to spine.cancel.ManagedProcess exists in this chunk.

observations.what: Function _anomaly_reason is defined but not used in this chunk; its usage is elsewhere.
Constants _ANSWER_FORMAT, _TRANSCRIPT_OPEN, _TRANSCRIPT_CLOSE are defined but not used in this chunk; they are used in _round_body.
Function _round_body builds a prompt string but does not include evidence; it defers to adapter for evidence placement.
The threading dispatch in _dispatch_round does not set daemon flag on threads nor implement a timeout cap in this chunk; the docstring claims they are daemons and abandoned at cap.
The _call function catches BaseException, which can include KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit; this may be too broad.
